competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Markets entered a dense policy week on a cautious footing: US equities remained elevated (Nasdaq 26,169, Dow 52,362, S&P 500 7,624) with the VIX near 19.5, while crude stayed firm (WTI 101.76, Brent 115.81) and gold held a defensive bid around 4,038. The US 10-year Treasury sat at 5.00% with yields broadly steady as investors balanced AI-related credit unease against safe-haven demand. Hormuz shipping risk and thin spare oil capacity keep the energy backdrop tense, even as LNG flows through the strait have improved. AI and private-credit headlines—stressed neocloud names and large debt raises for chips and data centres—are feeding the bid for duration and quality. Surveys point to a Bank of Canada move toward 2.50% on 28 October; Japan is expected to hold this week but sound hawkish after September’s call-rate step-up. New Zealand inflation could not be verified, so NZ-specific new risk stays off the board. Next: Federal Reserve and Bank of Canada decisions on 28 October, Bank of Japan messaging, megacap earnings, and whether oil and AI-credit jitters spill into broader risk appetite.

causal.assumptions_right: The CA-JP carry gap was real and paid. CADJPY isolated CA versus JP better than USD legs. BoJ did not hike during the hold. Flattening after the ToT pillar broke, rather than riding carry into 28 Oct, matched the original reason for the trade.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Durability of oil as CAD fundamental support; speed of ToT failure versus still-positive carry; hawkish-hold BoJ communication as a JPY-positive offset; two-way BoC event risk once the commodity premise was gone; treating post-exit drift to 112.23 as information to re-engage.
causal.causal_divergence: P&L was earned while oil and carry still agreed with CA-over-JP. After the slide, the economic driver of the CAD leg decoupled from still-positive carry and still-firm spot. Price continued to work after the reason died; that is residual momentum, not confirmation of the original belief.
causal.future_implication: Cross-CAD risk requires a live ToT or policy gap that survives a from-flat test. Closed-trade P&L and a few extra CADJPY pips are not that gap. AUDCAD stays off-limits as a reverse. EURJPY needs EA evidence that is not in this tape, so the book stays empty.
causal.observed_reality: Oil slid and knocked out the CAD ToT pillar; the long was closed 26 Oct at 112.04 from 110.9 for +154437; spot is now 112.23; BoC is polled at 2.50 on 28 Oct; BoJ is expected to hold with a hawkish lean; CORRA 2.24 vs TONA 1.227 still funds the cross; WTI 101.76 and Brent 115.81 are the current oil marks, with the slide magnitude itself unknown.
causal.original_belief: Oil-supported Canadian terms of trade plus a funded CORRA-over-TONA carry would keep CAD bid against JPY while BoJ remained the easier G10 central bank, so long CADJPY was the clean non-USD expression of that gap.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With oil as a hard invalidation, the desk would have flattened on the slide, still banked the harvest, and still refused both a 112.23 CADJPY re-entry and an AUDCAD reverse. Given only the present tape—ToT pillar already called broken, BoC tomorrow, BoJ hawkish-hold—CADJPY would not be opened from flat.

postmortems.expression_assessment: CADJPY was the correct isolation of CA versus JP. Failure was not the pair choice and not a reason to migrate into AUDCAD or USD legs. The broken input was the CAD oil/ToT assumption inside an otherwise clean cross.
postmortems.future_rule: Into a BoC decision week, CADJPY and AUDCAD may be opened only as from-flat initiations with a live oil/ToT or policy differential; never as re-entry or reverse of a just-closed CADJPY long, and never on leftover pips after the pillar has already failed.
postmortems.lesson: After a CADJPY ToT-carry long is closed because oil impaired the CAD pillar, do not reopen CADJPY and do not reverse AUDCAD unless that exact cross would be initiated from a flat book on new, independent AU-CA or CA-JP evidence.
postmortems.sizing_assessment: Realized +154437 on a now-flat book. Notional, risk limit, and vol-scaled size are unknown (null) in this tape, so sizing can only be judged as non-catastrophic: the winner was harvested without leaving residual CADJPY into BoC.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The CA-over-JP relative-value thesis was right for the holding window while oil supported CAD and BoJ stayed easy. It became stale the moment the terms-of-trade pillar broke: carry alone was never the original reason to own CAD versus JPY into a home-bank meeting.
postmortems.timing_assessment: Entry on 2 Oct at 110.9 caught the funded move. Exit on 26 Oct at 112.04, one session before the 28 Oct BoC, was the right date once ToT support was gone. The subsequent print at 112.23 is leftover drift, not evidence the exit was early in decision-quality terms.
postmortems.what_failed: Oil/ToT was treated as a durable CAD pillar rather than a condition that can fail faster than policy. There was no pre-committed oil invalidation that forced an exit at the slide rather than after the pillar was already judged broken. Post-exit spot at 112.23 shows residual momentum after the reason died; that drift is a process trap, not a missed mandate to reopen into BoC week.
postmortems.what_worked: CADJPY isolated a funded CA-over-JP view (CORRA above TONA, oil-supported CAD terms of trade, BoJ still the easier central bank) without Fed beta. The 2 Oct entry at 110.9 was paid through 26 Oct at 112.04 for +154437. Holding the cross rather than a USDCAD/USDJPY box kept the P&L on the intended differential while oil and carry aligned.

cross-merchant.thesis: Stay flat. CADJPY at 112.23 is not a from-flat initiation into the 28 Oct BoC: the oil terms-of-trade pillar that justified owning CAD is already impaired, BoJ is an expected hold with a hawkish lean, and leftover carry (CORRA 2.24 vs TONA 1.227) plus 19 pips of post-exit drift are not a new CA-JP gap. AUDCAD 0.9854 has no independent AU-versus-CA policy, growth, or inflation differential in this tape, so buying or fading it would only be the mirror of the closed CAD-over-JPY expression. EURJPY 176.15 is the least-dirty non-USD way to isolate a hawkish BoJ against EA, but EA inflation, growth, and policy path are unknown here, so it is not funded.
